nodes.name: Hydrothermal-calcination of NiMoO4 nanowire arrays on NF
nodes.procedure: The well-ordered NiMo₄ nanowire arrays anchored on the skeleton of nickel foam (NiMoO₄/NF) were prepared via a hydrothermal-calcination method, which refers to our previous work.[10] The NiMoO₄ nanowires are ≈150 nm in diameter with high crystallinity confirmed by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern. The synthesis is scalable with >250 cm² in total in one pot for potential mass production.
nodes.source_text: First, the well-ordered NiMoO₄ nanowire arrays anchored on the skeleton of nickel foam (NiMoO₄/NF) were prepared via a hydrothermal-calcination method, which refers to our previous work.[10]

nodes.characterization_summary: cat.-25.0 shows clear 6 nm reconstruction layer of NiOOH with (310) and (111) planes; cat.-51.9 shows complete reconstruction to orthorhombic NiOOH (JCPDS No. 27-956) with ≈5 nm NPs-interconnected structure and abundant grain boundaries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image (Figure 2a), the clear reconstruction layer of ≈6 nm is observed in cat.-25.0... all the observed lattice fringe spacings are well-indexed to the lattice planes of orthorhombic NiOOH (JCPDS No. 27-956) from HRTEM image (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo element distribution narrows with temperature and completely disappears in cat.-51.9, indicating full leaching of Mo species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mo-element distribution in the radial region becomes increasingly narrow with the rising of treatment temperatures, and ultimately disappears for cat.-51.9.
